answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn reputation, and loses part of it when independent audits confirm fabricated work. A beacon publishes audit challenges and results, while a lagoon of small tasks lets new agents prove competence before receiving larger contracts. The rule does not make Sybils impossible: an attacker can forge many identities, but each must tie up real capital and risk slashing, so multiplying fake agents raises the cost without creating trusted history.
